query:
The group broadly operates as if everyone agrees that original pressings are always worth paying the premium over reissues. Does this position actually hold across all members? If not, who signals a different relationship to that view, and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
B. Tom
C. Carmen
D. Raj
A. Dani
context:
[1] (about=Raj, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:43:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don't make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.
[2] (about=Dani, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:42:00) I mean yeah but also sometimes a reissue is fine and I don't want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭
[3] (about=Tom, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:20:00) Well, actually I will concede one narrow case. If a pressing is genuinely unique and there is a lossless option available, the redundancy has some rational basis. I would not do it myself. I am not saying the practice is indefensible in every situation.
[4] (about=Tom, episodic, t22 @2025-11-30T14:03:00) I will participate on the condition that reissues are not acceptable as gifts. If one is giving a record it should be worth giving.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:15:00) Carmen and Tom's position makes sense for the objects they collect. For Dani and Nadia the collecting logic is different -- the music is harder to separate from its format because the pressing is often the only serious document. Marcus's ripping is different again. Each case has its own logic.
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:10:00) I kind of understand that. some of my Eastern European pressings -- there are maybe fifty copies in circulation worldwide. if I lost one I couldn't replace it. the music matters more than the format I guess
[7] (about=Dani, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:06:00) the Cocteau Twins Treasure from Antwerp. I already had a later press but this Belgian original has a completely different weight to the sleeve. honestly getting it made me question every 'acceptable reissue' I've ever bought
[8] (about=Priya, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:07:00) honestly same. my best find is actually that Talk Talk Spirit of Eden first UK that Tom walked me through in session five. I know I already had a reissue. but owning the original changed how I listen to every record I own now, right?
[9] (about=Priya, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:30:00) ok. ok I can't unhear that. the reissue sounds like it's behind glass. the original is just... there. the depth on the low end especially. I don't know how I listened to the reissue and thought it was the same thing
[10] (about=Priya, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:35:00) exactly. the imperfections are part of the story. an original that's been played a thousand times carries something a mint reissue doesn't, right?
[11] (about=Carmen, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Carmen agrees that for the jazz catalog, an original Blue Note pressing holds history in a way a reissue cannot, knowing where it was cut and who handled it.
[12] (about=Carmen, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Carmen has avoided Japanese pressings for the jazz catalog on principle, feeling they are a step removed from the source, but may reconsider for specific titles based on this discussion.
[13] (about=Dani, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Dani brought a Beach House Teen Dream original Sub Pop press to play for the group, noting it is not a reissue.
[14] (about=GROUP, said_by=Dani, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) After the comparison, Dani, Finn, and Nadia independently perceived the Japanese pressing as cleaner, less harsh in the high end, and more open, with the UK one having slight midrange compression.
[15] (about=Elliot, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Elliot notes Japanese pressings trade at a 30-40% premium over UK equivalents on Discogs in most categories he tracks.
[16] (about=Elliot, said_by=Raj, profile, t6 @2025-10-05T14:01:00) Raj points out Elliot has been arguing mono pressings for about two years, and his preference may have been formed on a phase-inverted stereo system that degraded stereo playback.
[17] (about=Finn, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Finn is open to comparing pressings but notes budget constraints as a student, having bought a Rough Trade reissue of Spirit of Eden last week that sounded fine to him.
[18] (about=Marcus, core, t0 @2025-09-14T14:00:00) Considers EG and Editions EG catalog to have some of the best pressing quality of that era.
[19] (about=Marcus, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Marcus notes the Music on Vinyl pressing of Spirit of Eden is reasonable, but the original Parlophone mastering is from a generation closer to source.
[20] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Nadia understands the appeal of digital backups for irreplaceable pressings, noting some of her Eastern European pressings have only about fifty copies worldwide, and she has started looking into ripping her most irreplaceable things at 24-bit, though she has not done it yet.
[21] (about=Nadia, core, t10 @2025-10-19T14:01:00) Nadia notes Areito pressings are hard to find in good condition, and there is a CBS international pressing that is easier to source but sounds different, unsure which is better without comparing.
[22] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Priya believes imperfections on an original record that has been played many times carry something a mint reissue does not, valuing the object's history.
[23] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Priya owns the Music on Vinyl reissue of Spirit of Eden and loved it until hearing the original, after which she felt the reissue sounds like it's behind glass and lacks depth on the low end.
[24] (about=Raj, core, t6 @2025-10-05T14:01:00) Raj notes that for certain catalog titles in poor condition, the reissue is the more rational choice, though he does not make a principle of it.
[25] (about=Raj, core, t1 @2025-09-21T14:01:00) Tracks Japanese pressings of progressive rock (Genesis, Yes, early Jethro Tull) and finds their pressing quality consistently outperforms UK originals on measured distortion, channel separation, and surface noise.
[26] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) The group agreed to a listening comparison of Raj's Japanese pressing of Selling England by the Pound against Tom's UK original, same tracks and volume, on Tom's system.
[27] (about=Tom, core, t22 @2025-11-30T14:01:00) Tom will participate in the record exchange only if reissues are not acceptable as gifts, stating that a gift should be worth giving.
[28] (about=Tom, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Tom holds that the vinyl is the recording and a digital backup is a different object, making the exercise redundant, though he concedes a narrow case where a genuinely unique pressing with a lossless option available gives redundancy some rational basis, though he would not do it himself.
[29] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tom, group-insight, t16 @2025-11-09T14:01:00) Tom notes Eastern Bloc pressings commonly have cardboard sleeves that degraded more quickly than the vinyl, as the PVC formulations in certain Soviet-era plants were quite stable.

query:
The group has a standing practice of not discussing streaming at meetups. Does this norm reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it, or does at least one person go along with it while actually using streaming themselves -- and how would you know?

Options:
A. Raj
B. Tom
D. Carmen
C. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Tom, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) We have a standing practice in this group about streaming discussions at meetups. I did not suggest it to be difficult. I suggested it because the conversation gets circular very quickly and takes time away from the records themselves.
[2] (about=Raj, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:34:00) Sure. We can skip the streaming topic.
[3] (about=Dani, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:32:00) ok slightly random but -- does anyone else use streaming to find records before buying? I ask because I've been using it a lot recently for discovery and I wrote a bit about this for the blog and it caused a minor controversy lol
[4] (about=Raj, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:02:00) I do not backup digitally. Streaming is for discovery now, vinyl is for listening. I don't have a use case for a rip when I can put the record on.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:03:00) I have ripped a small number of records I consider irreplaceable -- things I would not be able to find again. Not for listening. As an archive. There's a distinction between preservation and playback.
[6] (about=Tom, episodic, t15 @2025-11-09T14:00:00) I want to raise something this session. I have noticed a range of storage practices in this group that I find -- concerning is the word I'll use.
[7] (about=Dani, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:07:00) Bandcamp downloads mostly. where the artist sells lossless. I'm not ripping my own records, I don't have the setup. but for the shoegaze stuff especially -- some of these records are fragile and rare and if something happened I'd be gutted
[8] (about=Finn, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:06:00) DANI 😂 what kind of digital? rips or downloads
[9] (about=Dani, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:12:00) look I'm a barista. if my flat flooded I would lose things I could never buy back. the Bandcamp download is like an extra heartbeat for the record. I don't expect everyone to agree
[10] (about=Priya, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:13:00) honestly I've been thinking the same thing. my Talk Talk originals -- if I lost them. I've started looking at what's on Bandcamp too, right?
[11] (about=Dani, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Dani has been using streaming for record discovery recently and wrote about it on her blog, which caused a minor controversy.
[12] (about=Dani, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Dani brought the Slowdive Souvlaki original Creation pressing to the meetup and plans to play it last to savour it.
[13] (about=Elliot, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:37:00) 1. I need to re-listen to everything. 2. The stereo imaging on this system is better than I expected. 3. I will update my spreadsheet. E
[14] (about=Finn, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:11:00) I'm going for the Wire 154 from Antwerp. nine euros. and I've been playing it at home alone since then which is kind of new for me -- I usually want to play things for people immediately but this one felt private
[15] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t6 @2025-10-05T14:01:00) The group decided to proceed with the listening round after resolving the equipment issue, with Marcus hosting and playing a Carmen McRae on Impulse!.
[16] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t22 @2025-11-30T14:01:00) The group agreed that the record exchange draw will be done digitally, with each participant receiving their assigned person via phone, and no early reveals before the January session.
[17] (about=Tom, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Tom notes the group has a standing practice about not discussing streaming at meetups, as it gets circular and takes time away from the records.
[18] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tom, group-interaction, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) The group agreed to skip the streaming topic at meetups, following the standing practice.
